To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the peptide chain duration of gastrins influences their stability and tumor uptake, which is improved by the inhibition of NEP and ACE.

(1) gastrin analogues with a peptide chain length of 14 amino acids or shorter are suitable for (99m)Tcm-labeling and (2) gastrin analogs with a peptide chain of 10 amino acids or shorter have a high tumor uptake in mice, and that (3) this uptake can be enhanced by co-administration of NEP/CE inhibitor.

(99m)Tcm-labeled gastrins, which are known to bind to CCK2R, are internalized and metabolized by the CCK2R-mediated endocytic pathway in the tumor cells, but not by the NEP/ACE-mediated endocytic pathways.

the development of new radiopharmaceuticals for imaging of tumors and inflammation.

the 2- and 3-mer gastrins are the most stable peptides in vivo, and their uptake is not affected by NEP/ACE inhibition, while the 4-mer gastrin shows the lowest stability, and the uptake is significantly enhanced by NEP/ ACE-inhibition.
the expression of ACE and NEP in tumor tissue is variable, and the inhibition of these proteases can lead to a more stable radiotracer and improved tumor targeting in vivo.
the 2nd generation of 99m Tc-labeled gastrin derivatives is superior to the 1st generation in terms of stability, tumor accumulation and tumor-to-background ratio.
